Alex.feeling: Tense and cramped: Casey's Hawk gain looks hard to dispute, and Ellis's visit stories don't match the reveal, but I'm holding a secret that I can't use without exposing myself.

Blair.feeling: Messy and frustrating: several players' visit claims contradict the egg counts, so it's hard to tell who is lying.

Casey.feeling: Messy and frustrating: several players keep changing their claimed animals, and only my Hawk egg on Alex is solid evidence.

Drew.feeling: Messy round: the table's claims contradict each other, and I can't yet tell who is lying.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 feels shaky: I'm Meowfia, the Farm side is pinning Alex on a single Hawk egg, and Finley's shifting claims could be a useful cover for us.

Finley.feeling: Confusing and frustrating: the table keeps misreading the Eagle and Owl rules, and I got eggsecuted in round 1 on a contradiction that was really a misread.

Alex.note: Casey is the main accuser and claims a Hawk gain, so I'll throw one low card at Casey to try to eggsecute a Farm player.

Blair.note: Casey's Hawk gain on Alex is the only hard evidence, and Alex's Owl story has been shaky. I'm confident enough to throw two high cards at Alex; winning banks them at full value.

Drew.note: Casey's Hawk gain on Alex is the only hard egg, so I'll throw one low card at Alex.

Ellis.note: Finley has flip-flopped on claims (Owl, then Turkey) and wrongly denied my visit, so Finley is a fair target. I'll throw one wild there and let the table's votes on Alex stand.

Finley.note: Casey's Hawk gain on Alex is the only hard evidence, so I'm throwing one low card at Alex.

Alex.confusing: The Owl's egg rule was easy to misread: I initially thought the egg went to the Owl's own nest, and Casey and Drew argued the same way. The text says the egg goes to the player visited, which only became clear when I reread it.
Alex.fun: Round 1's day was a fun cross-examination: Finley's Eagle +2 couldn't be squared with their own denial of visits, and the table turned on them.
Alex.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players can verify claims without rereading rules. Some counts were easy to misread under pressure.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw at Casey, a Farm Hawk, based on little evidence, and I should have kept my cards and stayed quiet until the table had more facts. As Meowfia I also drew attention by pushing accusations, so I'd be more subtle.

Blair.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg rules were the hardest to pin down: the Owl egg goes to the player the Owl visits, which several players misread for a while. Confused players' reports also made claims hard to check.
Blair.fun: Round 1, when I was the Sphinx, I told the table a made-up Farm visit and the table largely believed it while the Meowfia pair was hidden.
Blair.change: I would make the egg-count rules for Owl and Eagle clearer in the role text, since most of the day went to arguing over those readings.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I was dead before the day ended and could not contribute visits; I would have given my Eagle result to the table earlier if I had survived. Better to have spoken it on my first turn.

Casey.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg rules were hard to parse mid-day, since the Owl's egg goes to the player visited, not the Owl, and I got it wrong publicly for a round.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when my Hawk visit on Alex paid an egg and the table converged on the throw, ending with Alex eggsecuted and my team winning.
Casey.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about which visitor or egg source caused each change, so players can check claims without guessing.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw at Alex on weak evidence and wasted cards, when I should have held my high cards and waited for a verifiable claim.

Drew.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg rules were the hardest to read, since "their" and who gains the egg took several rereads. I also misread the Owl rule myself and had to retract it on day two.
Drew.fun: Round 3 was satisfying: Casey's Hawk gain on Alex was the only hard egg, and the table followed it to a correct throw that won the round.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which nest an egg went into, so players don't argue over Owl and Turkey gains.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I joined the throw at Finley, who was Farm, and I never tested Blair, who was the Sphinx Meowfia. I'd instead have asked Blair for their visit and egg details before throwing.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl's egg rule was easy to misread: it goes to the player the Owl visits, and several of us, me included, argued about whose nest it hit. Confused reports also made it hard to tell who was honest when a claim didn't add up.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when I was the Mouser and Blair was winked, then Casey's Kookaburra story fell apart and the table converged on a throw that worked. Watching egg counts pick apart the claims was the most satisfying part.
Ellis.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so counting eggs against claims isn't guesswork.
Ellis.regret: In Round 1 I threw at Finley on a weak read and then backed off, which left my team with a wasted throw. I'd rather have stayed quiet until the Eagle count was verified.

Finley.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg rules were easy to misread mid-day, and I spent several beats arguing about whose nest got the egg. Once I quoted the text, the table still kept misreading it.
Finley.fun: Round 3 was satisfying: my unchanged Turkey nest became hard evidence that Ellis and Blair were lying about visiting me. Calling the vote on Casey's Hawk gain then got Alex eliminated as Meowfia.
Finley.change: I would make the egg-gain rules for Owl, Eagle, and Turkey more explicit on the card, since most of the day's confusion came from people reading them differently.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I threw at Drew with a low card on a shaky read, and I got thrown at for it. Next time I would throw at nobody or wait for a clearer contradiction before throwing.

review.title: Blair Banks Big
review.headline: Blair won round one by throwing at the Turkey, then coasted to 43.
review.summary: Blair, a lone Sphinx in round 1, learned who the Turkey was. Blair threw three cards at that Farm player, and the table's own mistaken vote on Finley still gave Blair 15 points. Blair then led all game. A Mouser Wink killed Blair in round 2, but Blair still banked a big throw in round 3 and finished far ahead of everyone. The table spent most of its time arguing about what the animals do, and not much on who was lying.

rounds.recap: Finley (Eagle) was suspected because the table misread how the Eagle gains eggs. Finley's reading was correct and several players admitted it, but the vote still landed on Finley. Blair, the only Meowfia, threw at Ellis and won 15 points anyway, because the Farm vote on Finley ended the round as a Meowfia win.

Meowfia Ellis used the Mouser Wink to kill Blair, the score leader. The day turned into an argument about the Owl and Turkey rules. Casey was confused and had an unexplained +2, so everyone, including the two Meowfia, piled on Casey and eggsecuted a Farm player.

Casey's Hawk egg from visiting Alex was real evidence. Alex, a Sphinx, could not refute it. Everyone except Ellis threw at Alex, Alex was eggsecuted, and Farm won. Blair threw two 12s and banked 24 points.

highlights.text: Blair, knowing Ellis was the Turkey, threw three cards at a certain Farm player and took 15 points while the table piled onto Finley.
Ellis used the Mouser Wink on Blair, the leader, before anyone had spoken.
Casey's Hawk egg on Alex was clean evidence, and the table acted on it at once.
Blair threw two 12s at Alex and banked 24 points, which put the game out of reach.

confusions.what: Said the Owl gain looked off for Drew's Hawk claim and doubted Finley's Eagle gain, though Eagle gains per visitor to the player it visits.
Thought Ellis the Turkey should have gained eggs from Blair's visit. Visitors gain, not the Turkey.
Said Finley's +2 was short because Casey had three visitors. The Eagle does not count itself.
Said Finley's +2 needed visitors to Finley, then later said the Eagle counts Casey's visitors. Mixed up who the Eagle counts.
Said the Owl's egg goes to the Owl's own nest, and that the Owl's egg could not explain his +1.
Said a Turkey gains from visitors, and used that to explain Drew's +1.
Said the Owl egg goes to the Owl's own nest, then corrected herself.
Said Drew had to be the Turkey for the Owl's egg to be explained. In fact the Owl egg and the Turkey egg both landed on different nests, and Finley misread which was which.
Said Hawk and Meowfia hits were the only hard evidence, while ignoring that Drew's Falcon read on Ellis had already been verified.
Said a Turkey always gives its visitor an egg, so Finley could not be the Turkey. Finley was hugged, so the egg never happened.
Said Ellis's claimed visit was impossible because no egg came. The Floofer hug blocked the Turkey effect.
Said Ellis visiting a Turkey should have gained an egg. The hug blocked it.

worked: The Hawk gives a clean, checkable result. Casey's egg on Alex was the one piece of hard evidence all game, and it decided round 3.
The Mouser Wink created a real moment. Ellis killed the leader on beat 1 of round 2, which showed how strong a mid-day kill can be.
Throws are public in count but hidden in value, and that kept real choices alive. Blair's two 12s in round 3 were a clear bet on a confident read.
problems: Round 1's vote was decided by a rules misreading, not by lies. Finley's Eagle count was right, yet the table threw at Finley anyway. Fix: add a short in-app reminder of each animal's rule, or show each player their own role's exact effect at dawn.

Blair's 15-point round-1 win came from a single secret. A lone Meowfia who knows a Farm role can throw at a player who is surely Farm. High throws from the winning side make one round decisive. Consider capping the pile value, or making the banked cards less decisive.

Hugged and confused effects are invisible to the table, so valid reports looked like lies. Finley, Ellis, Blair and Drew all argued from egg counts that the hug had blanked. Fix: tell the hugged player at dawn that they were hugged.

Meowfia don't know each other, so in round 2 both Meowfia threw at Casey, the same Farm player, and in round 3 Ellis threw at Finley while Alex threw at Casey. Meowfia play was mostly passive. Few deceptions had any bite. Consider giving Meowfia a way to find each other, or a stronger night action.
Dead Blair still threw 0 for round 2 but banked high-value cards in round 3 and led by 30 points. After round 1 the game was effectively over. Add a catch-up rule, or scale the points per round.
